name: ESP32 Passive Wi-Fi Scanner
chip_detected: ESP32-D0WD-V3, revision 3.1 (recorded during prior board bring-up)
difficulty_reason: Uses the ESP32 Wi-Fi API and serial output; no external circuit or third-party library is required.
antenna_attachment_note: The user owns the supplied external antenna. Its connector state was not separately photographed during testing; repeated successful RF scans demonstrate that the board's receive path was functioning.

validation.standalone_serial_diagnostic: Passed; clean serial output observed through 32 sequential messages, reaching 32524 ms uptime, with no malformed characters or unexpected restart in the supplied screenshot.
validation.scanner_retest: Passed; fresh scanner run showed multiple consecutive readable scan tables at 115200 baud, with no malformed characters in the supplied retest output.
validation.reset_observation: ESP32 bootloader log appeared after the user manually reset/reconnected the board; user confirmed this was intentional, not an unexpected runtime reset.
validation.earlier_serial_noise: Not reproduced in the standalone serial diagnostic or subsequent scanner retest. Its original cause was not conclusively determined.
validation.privacy: Nearby SSID names omitted from public evidence.
validation.evidence: User-provided Serial Monitor screenshot and text from the standalone serial diagnostic and repeated physical Wi-Fi scans; actual nearby SSIDs are not retained in this metadata.

operating_scope: Original ESP32 Wi-Fi scans 2.4 GHz only; 5 GHz is outside this board's radio capability.
Passive scanning may miss weak or intermittent access-point beacons.
Scan count and RSSI vary with radio environment, antenna orientation and location.
